instruction: I want to set my Chrome homepage to https://www.wikipedia.org. Please configure the startup page or homepage button setting in Chrome settings so that this URL is set as my homepage.

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting the Chrome homepage to 'https://www.wikipedia.org'. The evaluator uses a custom getter get_chrome_homepage__9d2ba16da21ed7a3bc9ce454107b63a8 to extract the homepage URL from Chrome's Preferences file (session.startup_urls or homepage field) and compares it against the expected URL using exact_match. The postconfig restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are saved.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly checks both homepage field and all startup_urls entries (chrome.py:42-53), addressing the instruction's flexibility of 'startup page OR homepage button setting'
Flexible substring matching (lines 45, 52) allows the getter to correctly identify the expected URL even with URL variations (e.g., trailing slashes, www prefix)
exact_match metric (general.py:41-48) appropriately compares the extracted URL against the expected value
Postconfig includes 2-second sleep before pkill (lines 34-38), which gives Chrome time to flush preferences to disk, then restarts Chrome to verify persistence
Expected value 'https://www.wikipedia.org' correctly matches the instruction requirement
Minor concern: The 2-second sleep may not always be sufficient for Chrome to persist preferences on slower systems, but this is a practical trade-off and should work in most cases
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider increasing the initial sleep to 3-4 seconds for more robust preference persistence on slower systems
The getter could be more explicit in its return logic - currently returns first match found or falls back to startup_urls[0] or homepage, which might be confusing but functionally works
